channel.title: Gumshoe News Radio (Harry)
channel.description: Private AM-radio-style news bulletins for Londonderry, NH.
channel.itunes:author: Gumshoe

item.title: Oct 14 Evening - 1. Londonderry Weather
item.description: Good evening, and welcome to Gumshoe News Radio. It's Wednesday night, October fourteenth, and here's your Londonderry forecast from the National Weather Service. Tonight, partly cloudy, with a low around forty-six and a light northwest breeze. Tomorrow, Thursday, it's sunny and cooler, with a high near fifty-nine. Clouds move in Thursday night, with a low around forty. Looking ahead: Friday is a rain day, with a hundred percent chance and a high near sixty-two, and showers likely Friday night with gusts up to twenty-five miles an hour. Saturday clears out, but it's chilly, with a high near forty-seven, and Saturday night dips to about twenty-nine, so it may be time to bring in the plants. Sunday, sunny and fifty-three. Then a nice warm-up: Monday sixty-two, Tuesday sixty-four, and next Wednesday, sunny and sixty-two.

item.title: Oct 14 Evening - 2. Top US News
item.description: Now, the top stories here at home. Inflation picked up in September, with consumer prices rising at a three point seven percent annual rate, driven largely by gasoline, according to the government report covered by the Wall Street Journal and Reuters. Stocks fell on worries the Federal Reserve may raise rates again. Kimberly Guilfoyle has resigned as U.S. ambassador to Greece, days after the Journal reported she asked a Republican donor to pay off a hundred-thousand-dollar credit card bill. On the campaign trail, President Trump flew to Alaska to help save a Republican Senate seat, according to the Washington Post, and the Associated Press reports Republicans are pulling back from several front-line House districts. In Maine, Senator Susan Collins debated her Democratic challenger, Troy Jackson. And in Pennsylvania, a sixth person has died of measles, as cases there top eleven hundred. The C.D.C. is sending more help.

item.title: Oct 14 Evening - 3. World News
item.description: Around the world. The Vatican says Pope Leo the Fourteenth, who is seventy-one, has been diagnosed with lung cancer, and had successful surgery on Tuesday at Rome's Gemelli hospital to remove part of his right lung. His appointments are cancelled through October twentieth. In the Middle East, Yemen's Houthis attacked the headquarters of Saudi Aramco in Dhahran, causing a fire, after Saudi strikes in Yemen. Reuters reports two ships sank near the Strait of Hormuz after being hit, and Brent crude settled above a hundred and six dollars a barrel. In Ukraine, Russian strikes left about six hundred thousand people without power, according to President Zelensky. Separately, Ukraine says new Starlink limits are disrupting its drone missions. And in Congo, the Ebola outbreak has passed nine thousand confirmed cases, the largest in the country's history, while Kenya has reported a second case.

item.title: Oct 14 Evening - 4. From Your X Feed
item.description: Now, a look at what's buzzing in your X feed this evening. The White House account promoted what it calls America's golden age of science, featuring tech leaders including Jensen Huang, Lisa Su, Satya Nadella, Michael Dell and Elon Musk. It was one of the most-liked posts in your timeline tonight. Midterm energy is everywhere. Senator Mike Lee, posting as at Based Mike Lee, urged Ohio voters to back Senator Jon Husted. And Vivek Ramaswamy posted from a stop in Akron, which he called the Rubber Capital of the World. At Tyler Bowyer says he's hearing about seventy-five thousand ballots came in today in Maricopa County, Arizona. That's his claim, and it isn't confirmed. On the markets side, at Trung T Phan noted that Apple's market value closed above five trillion dollars for the first time. And in entertainment, Variety reports Full House star Jodie Sweetin says her co-star Dave Coulier is doing great after his cancer battle.

item.title: Oct 14 Evening - 5. Local News & Events
item.description: Closer to home, in Londonderry. The Londonderry Historical Society hosts an open house this Sunday, October eighteenth, from one to three, with tours of the Morrison House, the Parmenter barn, and the Clark blacksmith shop, plus period military drills with musket firing. The Londonderry Times reports a busy stretch for local firefighters earlier this month, with two house fires and a medical helicopter call at the high school, and the department is reminding everyone to check their smoke alarms. And a civic reminder: the general election is Tuesday, November third. New Hampshire closes registration six to thirteen days before, so check with the Town Clerk, or register at your polling place on Election Day.

item.title: Oct 14 Evening - 6. Uplifting Story
item.description: And finally, a little hero story, from WDIV in Detroit. Five-year-old Hudson Tenn was with his grandmother and his three-year-old sister when his grandmother collapsed. He tried to find her car keys, couldn't, so he ran down the street for help, while making sure his little sister stayed safe. Good samaritans and deputies stepped in, and his grandmother, Terri, recovered. Today, township officials and the county sheriff's office are honoring Hudson with an award for bravery. Terri put it simply: he's my hero. That's your news for now. This is Gumshoe News Radio. Just message me if you'd like more on any story.
